deck: PERCEIVED OWNERSHIP, PROVISIONAL FILINGS AND ASSIGNMENT RECORD SEARCHES
ROYALTY RATES, ANNUAL MINIMUMS AND EXCLUSIVE VERSUS NON-EXCLUSIVE GRANTS
site_ui.lead: Patent attorneys, licensing coaches and product founders show how to keep title, file a provisional for perceived ownership, and license an invention for 2 to 10% of wholesale backed by annual minimums instead of floating $250,000 in inventory.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies, with every quote carrying timestamped inline attribution to its channel and video. The chapters run from choosing a licensing business model through royalty administration to licensing digital IP, AI data and software.
chapters: Find Licensees and Pitch the Product
Negotiate the License and Term Sheet
Administer, Audit and Account for Royalties
License Digital IP, AI Data and Software
flow: Run concept-based Boolean searches with parentheses, confirm the exact application number, and pull assignment records for current owners and security interests
File a provisional for perceived ownership at the $65 micro entity rate, disclosing every implementation detail and paying the fee the same day
Weigh licensing against assignment and manufacturing, and manufacture only with strong demand, healthy margins, a clear sales channel and operating capacity
Approach manufacturers as a product developer with polished brochures, formal letters and prototypes, never paying a broker upfront fees
Lock price, annual minimums and a refusal to indemnify before the first meeting, settling price last against the licensee's next best alternative
Keep title, pick exclusive or non-exclusive grants carefully, and tier royalties at 7% granted, 5% pending and 1% if the patent never issues
